newsitem.title: HUNGARY: LUFTHANSA FLIES 34T OF OPIUM INTO BUDAPEST.
newsitem.headline: LUFTHANSA FLIES 34T OF OPIUM INTO BUDAPEST.

text.p: German national airline Deutsche Lufthansa AG flew a Boeing B747-200F cargo airplane into Budapest Ferihegy Airport on Friday to deliver 34 tonnes of Indian opium worth over $2.0 million, the airline's handling agent Malev Rt told Reuters.
Malev, or Magyar Legikozlekedesi, is the Hungarian national airline, but it also handles cargo and passengers for most planes flying into Budapest.

The opium, which will be refined in Hungary for the domestic pharmaceutical industry, arrived in Budapest under heavy security on a flight normally scheduled non-stop to Frankfurt from New Delhi. Lufthansa diverted the plane to Budapest to simplify delivery of the opium.
The plane, which was carrying over 100 tonnes of cargo, also unloaded some garments and handicrafts in Budapest before continuing to Frankfurt with the remaining freight, Malev said.
